entities.summary: Tudor Arghezi was a Romanian writer and political figure, widely considered one of his country's greatest poets. An illegitimate, part-Hungarian child who was purposely vague about his roots, he had a troubled youth during which he held a variety of jobs—including a stint as a hierodeacon of the Romanian Orthodox Church, from which he gathered his extreme anti-clericalism. He debuted in the 1890s as an affiliate of the Symbolist movement, being welcomed as an outstanding poet. Arghezi renounced this career to study theology in Switzerland, but never graduated, training instead as a watchmaker and typographer.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Tudor Arghezi's poetry played a significant role in shaping Romania's cultural identity during the early 20th century, influencing generations of writers and intellectuals. His work continues to be studied and celebrated in Romania today.
